context: This prompt requests creation of a seed script that validates and recreates required RDD instance files and folders. The script should check against manifest.json requirements and recreate missing mandatory items using convention files. Questions help clarify implementation details and error handling strategies.

questions.question-text: Should the seed script create missing folders recursively or stop at the first missing parent folder?

options.label: Create folders recursively (like mkdir -p)
options.pros: More robust, handles any missing parent folders automatically, prevents partial initialization
options.cons: May silently create unexpected folder structures if paths are misconfigured

options.label: Require all parent folders to exist first
options.pros: More explicit, catches configuration errors early, ensures intentional setup
options.cons: More fragile, requires multiple script runs or manual intervention

questions.recommendation-rationale: Recursive folder creation is standard for initialization scripts and aligns with the goal of automatic seeding during web server startup. It ensures the script can fully initialize the instance without manual intervention.

questions.question-text: How should the seed script handle existing files that need to be recreated?

options.label: Skip existing files entirely (preserve user modifications)
options.pros: Protects user data and customizations, safe for repeated runs
options.cons: Won't fix corrupted or malformed existing files

options.label: Validate existing files and recreate only if invalid
options.pros: Fixes corrupted files, ensures file format compliance
options.cons: More complex, requires validation logic for each file type

options.label: Always overwrite existing files
options.pros: Ensures files match current conventions, simplest implementation
options.cons: Destroys user modifications, data loss risk

questions.recommendation-rationale: Preserving existing files is safest and aligns with the manifest's upgrade policy ('preserve' for .rdd-instance). The seed script should only create missing files, not modify existing ones, to avoid data loss.

questions.question-text: What should the seed script do when it cannot find a convention file referenced in manifest.json?

options.label: Fail immediately with error message
options.pros: Clear feedback, prevents incorrect initialization, forces fix of configuration issues
options.cons: Script cannot complete partial seeding, may block web server startup

options.label: Log warning and create empty file
options.pros: Allows script to continue, enables web server to start
options.cons: Creates invalid files, may cause runtime errors later

options.label: Log warning and skip that file
options.pros: Allows partial seeding, doesn't create invalid files
options.cons: Leaves instance in incomplete state, may cause runtime errors

questions.recommendation-rationale: Missing convention files indicate a framework installation problem that should be fixed immediately. Failing fast prevents creating an invalid instance state and makes the problem visible to the developer.

questions.question-text: Should the seed script validate the structure of files it creates (e.g., verify JSON is valid)?

options.label: Yes, validate all created files
options.pros: Ensures files are well-formed, catches template errors early
options.cons: More complex, requires validation logic for each file format

options.label: No, trust convention files are correct
options.cons: May create invalid files if convention templates are malformed

questions.recommendation-rationale: Validation provides immediate feedback if convention files have errors. Since this runs during web server initialization, catching problems early prevents runtime failures and improves developer experience.

questions.question-text: How should the seed script report its actions to the user?

options.label: Print detailed log of all actions (created folders, files, skipped items)
options.pros: Full transparency, helpful for debugging, clear audit trail
options.cons: Verbose output may clutter web server startup logs

options.label: Print summary only (count of created items)
options.cons: Less visibility into what was actually done

options.label: Silent mode unless errors occur
options.cons: No confirmation that seeding ran successfully

questions.recommendation-rationale: Detailed logging helps developers understand what the seed script is doing, especially during initial setup or troubleshooting. Since it runs only once during web server initialization, verbose output is acceptable.

questions.question-text: Should the seed script be idempotent (safe to run multiple times)?

options.label: Yes, must be idempotent and safe for repeated execution
options.pros: Safe for web server restarts, can fix missing files later, developer-friendly
options.cons: Must handle all edge cases carefully

options.label: No, designed for one-time initialization only
options.pros: Simpler implementation, can assume clean state
options.cons: Cannot fix missing files after initial setup, fragile

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt explicitly states the script should 'check and do nothing' once seeded, and run during 'each initialization' of the web server. This clearly requires idempotent behavior for safe repeated execution.

questions.question-text: The prompt contains contradictory instructions about template files. Section 'Template Files to Create' requests creating template files in .rdd/templates/, but the Notes section states 'No template files are used - the files content is generated by the script'. How should the seed script generate file content?

options.label: Create template files in .rdd/templates/ and use them to generate instance files
options.pros: Separates template content from code, easier to customize file headers/structure, templates are reusable
options.cons: More files to maintain, adds complexity, template location not in manifest.json

options.label: Generate file content directly in code based on convention files (no templates)
options.pros: Simpler implementation, follows 'convention over configuration', no extra files needed, aligns with manifest.json structure
options.cons: File structure is hardcoded in Python, less flexible for customization

options.label: Read convention files and extract/generate minimal valid content from them
options.pros: Fully convention-driven, no hardcoded content, adapts to convention changes
options.cons: Complex parsing logic required, convention files are documentation not templates

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option B aligns with the Notes section stating 'no template files are used' and with the manifest.json structure which references convention files (which are documentation, not templates). Generating minimal valid content in code is simpler and follows the 'convention over configuration' principle mentioned in the prompt.
